outcomes: A workload declares its services once and resolves them from one container tree that spans the application and its modules
A broken dependency graph fails while the application is being composed, not on the first request that needs it
Request-scoped state is isolated per scope while shared state stays shared
Shutdown disposes every constructed instance after the consumers that depend on it
nonGoals: Deriving providers from decorators, reflection metadata, or type inference
Hot-swapping a provider in a started container outside the explicit fork and refresh surfaces
Promising that a pre-1.0 minor release keeps the previous injection contract

requirements.text: Starting a container context validates the whole registered graph first: an unresolvable dependency, a dependency cycle, or an unmet module requirement fails before any instance is constructed.
A singleton provider is constructed at most once per container, including when several asynchronous resolutions of the same token overlap.
A scoped provider is constructed once per scope, is the same instance for every resolution inside that scope, and is never shared with another scope, including concurrent ones.
A provider registered as private resolves only inside the container that declared it and is not reachable from a parent or sibling container.
Closing a context runs onClose hooks in reverse construction order, and resolving a token after close fails instead of returning a disposed instance.
A context starts once and closes once: starting twice, closing before start, and resolving before start each raise a named error.
The package root exports only the stable injection surface; test doubles are reachable from the testing subpath and container escape hatches from the inject subpath.
